朝鮮總督府

文也 花椒潤蔬菜乃至各隨其事成歲月水有早早晩不必

乾陰暴乾者放之日中晒也陰乾者謂不露日暴如水

採藥法 以二月八月至春秋技葉乾粘調潤

月乾韓者並宜火肉乾韓十

二陰者已後日乾韓者並宜火肉乾井佳乾乃十月好韓〇諸藥八月已前采者乃可採

者已後日乾者悉宜易得多惡日良至月曝如水

木根草雖陰都乾乃令按乾已令壊采者乃火乾者悉宜易得十惡日良至月
translation:
Dongui Bogam (Treasured Mirror of Eastern Medicine), Herbal Medicine Section, Volume One

[Stamp: Chosŏn Government-General Hospital Library]

Composed by Royal Physician of Loyal, Diligent, Upright, and Bright merit, Holder of the Senior First Rank, Duke of Yangpyeong, Heo Jun, by Royal Command

Introductory Examples for Decoctions

Methods of Gathering Medicines

[The text discusses methods of drying medicinal herbs:]

"Shade-drying" means to dry without exposing to direct sunlight — as when water [moisture] is involved, [the herbs] must not be rushed.

"Sun-drying" (暴乾) means to place [the herbs] in direct sunlight to dry in the sun.

As for gathering medicines: In the 2nd and 8th months — that is, spring and autumn — stems, leaves, dry [material], and adhesive [substances] should be collected and processed. [Herbs gathered] in the 2nd month and dried in the shade should be dried over fire if needed; [those gathered] in the 10th month are best. As for all medicines gathered before the 8th month, they may then be collected. Those gathered after that date that are sun-dried are easily obtained, though of inferior quality, until the good months come.

Roots of trees and grasses, even if shade-dried throughout, should be pressed when dry. Material already deteriorated that is gathered should be dried over fire; such material is easily obtained but inferior, until the good months.

text:
三品藥性

上藥一百二十種為君主養命以應天無毒多服久服不傷人欲輕身益氣不老延年者本上經

中藥一百二十種為臣主養性以應人無毒有毒斟酌其宜欲遏病補虛羸者本中經

下藥一百二十五種為佐使主治病以應地多毒不可久服欲除寒熱邪氣破積聚愈疾者本下經

三品合三百六十五種法三百六十五度一度應一日以成一歲倍其數合七百三十名也

六陳良藥

吳茱萸 狼毒 枳實 陳橘皮 半夏 麻黃

右六種藥欲得陳久者良以其性烈恐傷人也新者其氣烈聚精神須陳久方可和緩其勢一陳黃昏

修製法

凡修製藥在乎病主治在乎藥勢一流者不要在乎病酒治在乎手藥面及

吳茱萸家多用之者手治宜半夏皮炒盡其勢不變可也幾病在咽下膈膜上者

松皮須用酒洗以製毒大病者須炒大黃者須知如胃下氣藥也久弱之則烏之粉半

子須炮以制毒也生須用酒浸暴乾恐寒傷胃氣也熟地黃也久

人須合用之酒浸也暴乾
translation:
Three Grades of Medicinal Properties

Upper-grade medicines, 120 kinds, serve as sovereign drugs that nourish life in accordance with Heaven. They are non-toxic, and taking them in large amounts or over a long period does not harm people. These are for those who wish to lighten the body, boost energy, resist aging, and extend life. These are recorded in the Upper Classic.

Middle-grade medicines, 120 kinds, serve as minister drugs that nourish one's nature in accordance with Humanity. They may or may not be toxic, and one must judge their appropriate use carefully. These are for those who wish to suppress illness and supplement weakness. These are recorded in the Middle Classic.

Lower-grade medicines, 125 kinds, serve as assistant and courier drugs that treat disease in accordance with Earth. Most are toxic and should not be taken for long periods. These are for those who wish to eliminate cold, heat, and pathogenic qi, break up accumulations, and cure illness. These are recorded in the Lower Classic.

The three grades together total 365 kinds, corresponding to 365 degrees, one degree for each day, forming one year. Doubled, the total comes to 730 names.

Six Aged Excellent Medicines

Evodia fruit (吳茱萸), Wolfsbane (狼毒), Unripe bitter orange (枳實), Aged tangerine peel (陳橘皮), Pinellia (半夏), Ephedra (麻黃)

These six medicines are best when aged and old, because their nature is fierce and may harm people when fresh. When fresh, their qi is concentrated and intense; only after aging do they become mild and gentle in their potency.

Methods of Processing and Preparation

In all processing and preparation of medicines, the key lies in understanding the disease; the governing of treatment lies in the power of the medicine. For certain flowing conditions, the concern is not merely the disease; wine-based treatment depends on the hand's technique as well.

Evodia (吳茱萸) is commonly used in households; for treatment, it is appropriate to stir-fry Pinellia until the outer skin is fully processed and its potency is moderated. For diseases located below the throat and above the diaphragm:

Pine bark must be washed with wine to neutralize its toxicity. For serious illness, one must stir-fry. For rhubarb (大黃), one must know that it is a medicine for descending stomach qi. For prolonged weakness, it is charred to powder.

Seeds must be blast-roasted to neutralize toxicity. Fresh ones must be soaked in wine and sun-dried, lest cold damage the stomach qi. As for prepared rehmannia (熟地黃), used over a long period —

They must be combined and used together, soaked in wine and sun-dried.

text:
火酒浸泡湯亦然熬炒當歸製其毒也發散之意也九蒸九曝者製酥灸者行用

肝經以浸絲醋也製入便腸製入香附置製法入必用用當便入

降浸佐水薑一用以煮汁宿虛乾以九童香便則性爆製入香膽製以必用用童盐者行用

斫以佐水煮以木以童香便則性爆製入香膽製以酒煮以醋煮者便入

之斫理也當歸地須黃用亦然製疲疲以絡滯而世實鹽盐以水血者以酒煮以醋煮便入

傷白門實懸用湯半浸夏製多殺其不數味疲疲以造病薑計浸透則以尊腎問無補元氣升補疏便入

仁猪大冬麻蓮子盆烏藥智類之不去類不心令人煩躁人心志巴子戰蟾汁源

去當茯麻地芡補補草果去皮則令人滿閱鮮桃元痞補氣

湯去雙仁及其皮尖則不生麻疹泡薑去半夏茯苓半夏陳皮桃仁氣

則參不能通山去豆解毒帶不鼓見功花草果消無醋
translation:
This passage is from a Chinese herbal medicine text (Dongui Bogam, Liquid Medicines section) describing methods of processing and preparing medicinal herbs. The content covers:

Huojiu (grain alcohol) is used for soaking and steeping; decoctions are similarly prepared by boiling. Stir-frying and processing with Danggui (Angelica sinensis) removes toxicity and promotes dispersal. Nine times steaming and nine times sun-drying is a method of processing; roasting with clarified butter (su) is another preparation method for use.

For liver channel medicines: soaking in vinegar is a processing method. Entering the intestines requires specific preparation. Xiangfu (cyperus) is prepared and placed accordingly; the preparation method must be used with童便 (boys' urine) and salt for administration.

For reducing stagnation: using water with ginger, boiling with童便 (boys' urine), drying, processing with vinegar, soaking overnight for deficiency conditions is appropriate.

Regarding Danggui (Angelica): it guides to the blood, addresses fatigue and channel stagnation; used with salt water, boiled in wine or vinegar for administration.

For Banxia (Pinellia): processing removes toxicity; used to treat phlegm conditions. Soaking in ginger juice makes it transparent. It supplements the kidney, regulates qi, and promotes flow.

Regarding Renzhu, Fuling, Maren, Lianzi, Wuyao, Zhishi and similar herbs: improper preparation causes restlessness and agitation. Taoren (peach kernel) processed correctly resolves fullness.

Regarding double kernels and removing skin and tips from seeds to prevent rashes: soaking ginger, processing Banxia, Fuling, Chenpi, Taoren is done to regulate qi.

Regarding Shen (ginseng): if unable to move through, use Shanzha to resolve toxicity; Huacao fruit with vinegar eliminates this.

translation:
Coptis (Huanglian): According to the skin and herb [entries], it counteracts [certain substances], reduces pus and blood [accumulation], tonifies [the body]. With black morning glory (Heichou): it benefits the stomach and black [conditions]. With gardenia (Zhizi): it stops bleeding. With Sichuan Coptis (Chuanlian): it aids the seedling [of the herb] and treats distant [conditions]. With Yuanzhi (Polygala): it is non-toxic and reaches wind [conditions]. With dried Acorus (Chenpu): [used together].

Processing methods: Stir-fry or use in decoction to make it penetrate (e.g., with Mirabilite/saltpeter, stir-fry with brine, steam with bamboo juice, steam with ginseng antler and Huoxiang, stir-fry into Ten-Thousand Decoction, add to the decoction's medicinal steaming).

For removing toxins and treating sores from fire: use Evodia (Wuzhuyu) as the chief [herb]; use floating specimens for [addressing] upward [rising conditions]; use sinking specimens for [addressing] downward [conditions]; grind into fine powder; soak in milk to make pills; take with cinnabar.

Croton seed (Badou): take the kernel, two qian, remove the shell and oil; form into round pills; with cinnabar, one fen; fine powder applied to the scalp area for darkening and moistening; take the best sun-dried [preparation]; for sinews, moisten [them]; processed with Du [herb] for raw use.

For various medicinal preparations: stir-fry to remove the tendency to move without generating [new qi]; use fine powder for use; process with vinegar and Aconite accessory root (Fuzi) for various medicinal uses; stir-fry with vinegar to make the substance real; use the juice to stir-fry to remove [the tendency] to move without generating [new qi]; use fine powder for application; process with Eucommia (Du) for raw use.

text:
制藥方法

方為定法　須釀酒　炒用茶連　須涿子　洗之　在下　生用　顏面　九

手皮膚者　而　熟藥降生　燥升　以

方制君臣　謂何也　謂岐伯曰　主病之謂君　佐君之謂臣　應臣之謂使　非此對　病之善惡道　以上日　中下之病　三品

君佐日三　飼日　道品　當何從臣　此對為日之佐　為臣之應　法病明以　善道惡則　不珠貴品

也謂帝希　佐君　之方　從臣　此對為法　病以非　上日中　下三之謂品

也之調　以主贊病者　為君也　佐君者　為臣也　使臣者為佐　君藥有應臣之　以佐	之使　制又若多一　使君君三　相為必貴

宜官　使皆　擭皆熊　合以主　贊病成者　救一方用君　也佐君注	者為日佐　藥為臣之應　有臣之使　若可制　者最多　君多等　少三

臣宜多　佐亦少　則寡之不　周防藥君之　治於也　上證為君熟　若多者　人五　使臣之佐　用之制

臣臣　次邑少　佐佐則　寡力不　防周之也　治於藥　君熟黃附　苓為君　者最多　若可制多　君三少

臣多　佐之中域　熙假君令　連為藥君　又防治　風濕藥　君之己治　為上熟君　黃附苓　為君者

臣佐之　類是也　熙用五六　城陰陽　配合用君　於三四十分　外分有臣　根加藥減　數七同八

佐使石骨肉有單行者有相須者有相使者有相惡者有相反者有相殺者薑化寶草
translation:
Methods of Preparing Medicines

The fixed method of a formula requires fermented wine; stir-fry with tea and coptis; rinse with water; use raw below; use on the face; use nine [ingredients].

Regarding the skin and flesh, processed medicines descend and moisten, while raw medicines rise and dry.

On the method of sovereign, minister, assistant, and envoy in a formula: What does this mean? Qibo said: The herb that governs the disease is called the sovereign; that which assists the sovereign is called the minister; that which responds to the minister is called the envoy. It is not merely about whether the disease is mild or severe — this applies to the upper, middle, and lower classifications of disease, and to the three grades of medicines.

The sovereign, assistant, and the three daily doses; the feeding schedule; the grade of the preparation; following the ministers in responding — the assistant serves the minister, and the envoy responds to the minister; the method follows the severity of the disease; what is not inferior is considered of high grade.

The emperor asked what is meant by sovereign and assistant; the assistant of the sovereign is the minister; this method addresses disease; upper, middle, and lower — three grades are distinguished.

That which is called the chief praises the sick person — this is the sovereign; that which assists the sovereign is the minister; that which directs the minister is the assistant; the sovereign herb has ministers responding to it, using assistants and envoys. When composing a formula with many ingredients, if one sovereign, three ministers — they must be complementary and valued.

It is appropriate for the envoy to be numerous; when combining, the sovereign is the chief drug; those that support the disease become ministers; the assistant of the sovereign becomes the minister; the envoy of the minister is the assistant; if one makes a formula, the most numerous is the sovereign, and the ministers are many with few assistants.

When ministers are many and assistants few, the strength is insufficient to encompass prevention with medicine; the sovereign is processed, such as processed Coptis — the sovereign should be most numerous; if the formula has many, three sovereigns and few ministers.

With many ministers, in the middle domain, the sovereign of Coptis is used processed, and also for treating wind-damp; the sovereign herb processed — such as prepared Aconite and Poria — the sovereign is most numerous.

As for the ministers and assistants — this is the category. Using five or six processed [ingredients]; combining yin and yang, using the sovereign with three or four parts in ten; outside those parts there are ministers; adding ginger and reducing the count by seven, same as eight.

As for assistant and envoy herbs: there are those used alone (single action), those that are mutually reinforcing (mutual need), those that assist each other (mutual use), those that are mutually antagonistic (mutual aversion), those that counteract each other (mutual opposition), and those that neutralize each other's toxicity (mutual suppression). [Examples include] ginger, transforming [herbs], precious [herbs], and grasses.

text:
湯散丸法

有相惡者有須相反者有相發者惡九此七情合和時若或少有毒皆方

宜相當用也家制云可分相異非分兩勿謂合勿藥用也少九方

同繞繞方皆○言病分九者之不兩者合若方

屢溪日則每九君病愈之必兩分均若異佐使也養性品補

味丹用甘山草以施以無致其力吐寒不熟宜難○黃亦無用之以不不熟藥方性須品

大計用生何黃以非行護經實蜜通尊○子無何薑麻者以不通藥非盡其性須品

須燥用藥性有宜血補湯非罾子無何薑麻者以通結○竹瀝非不薑其性須

領用生熱無最便於清脬補尊○罾子無何薑麻者亦通結○竹瀝藥非盡

也麻如太麻茯苓煎者宜亦有一宜散薑者宜水煮者亦有不可入湯者

者者即亦胡麻茯苓煎也性如不得粟達趑越物散以○宜者亦有不宜煮

也如子如小豆者令赤小豆也以胡豆三六九大麻以二一大大如麻子唯之麻豆細

子也唯之如小豆者令赤小豆也以胡三六九散以為有云大大如細
translation:
Methods for Decoctions, Powders, and Pills

When medicinal ingredients have mutual aversion or mutual antagonism, or when they provoke each other's toxicity, these seven types of interactions (the "seven relations") must be considered when combining and harmonizing them. If any toxic substances are present, all formulas should use appropriate counterparts.

When preparing household formulas, one may divide the portions differently; the weights and measures listed are not to be rigidly treated as fixed — do not say "combine" or "use the drug" without thought. In nine-ingredient formulas, the portions should be balanced according to the role of sovereign, minister, and assistant herbs. When the illness improves, the balance of the two portions must be even.

Regarding the flavor of cinnabar and the use of sweetroot (licorice) and mountain herbs: if they are administered without careful dosing, they cannot bring out the full effect; if vomited up due to coldness or incompleteness, they are difficult to use. Yellow [ginger] also, when used without the proper method, will not pass through properly. Bamboo sap (zhuli) likewise, if not combined with ginger, its nature cannot be fully expressed.

When preparing medicines that are dry-natured, they should tonify the blood and aid the decoction; bamboo sap should not be used without ginger, as it will not move through properly.

For those like hemp seed (huma) and poria (fuling) that are to be decocted, some should be made into powder with ginger, some should be boiled in water, and some cannot be added to a decoction.

Some ingredients, like small red beans (chixiaodou) and hemp seeds, in formulas of three, six, or nine [units], large or small, coarse or fine — these distinctions must be carefully followed.

translation:
Regarding preparations the size of large soybeans: mix powder with honey; if it is the size of a firmiana (parasol tree) seed, use two large soybeans as the standard measure.
For a square-inch spoon of powder mixed with honey, two measures equal the size of a pellet; use two large soybeans as the standard.
For elderly patients, the standard formula uses seven-tenths; to achieve the proper measure, use nine [units] equaling two large soybeans as standard.

Regarding decoctions with medicine: adjust the knife-measure to seven parts; the correct formula is to take [the amount] equal to a firmiana seed — nine [units] equal to large soybeans as standard.

For rubbing applications of medicine: the formula states to use tiger [fat] as a base; take a standard amount equal to pine-firmiana seeds — nine [units] equal to large soybeans.

Regarding oral dosing: as stated, use hemp [seed size] as reference — one dose; six parts obtained; take [the amount] — not exceeding the standard; measure in two parts then decoct; raise to one [sheng]; ten yun [units] of powder.

For knife-measure decoctions: use bean-sized amounts; finely bite/crush; below one [unit]; six parts; eight fen; then one sheng of medicine; one sheng, ten yun of powder.

Water intake: use iron vessels; crush to fine powder; swallow with large amounts; bring together into a vessel; this is easily prepared as a powder poultice.

Stop [the medicine] when: the taste is removed, thinned; when disease is treated with congee; store in a repository; accumulate greatly; this is easily prepared — disperse, poultice, hemp; prepare as a decoction; this is the method. Ancient classic formula.

For the qi [vital energy]: large [dose] — exemption applies; rounded pills; combine with dregs; for storage accumulation; apply the qi; coarsely ground, fine, raw — make into a decoction; this is the preparation method.

For steaming [preparations]: use ginger juice; collect finely; prepare steamed cake.

For treating toxicity: use Arisaema (南星, nanxing); make into nine-and-a-half [pills]; take the desired [dose]; remove [impurities]; concentrate; wash; use raw ginger; store overnight; steam; make into a cake with the juice; collect finely.

text:
七方

者取易化也煉蜜而者旋取其
遇化也清水給九湯者也又九者久病難取徐徐散而旋治
效化壞用之大抵湯者緩也不能速去病之用取
即之意也大小者緩急也方閉丹者緩也不也九者又易化也煉
七方九之也。七方之君二者也大三方即小方也君一臣二方即補下也門
○七方九二者大小君一臣二方即缓不大方也奇一方也緩而厭頻乃而也君小臣二方即複方也小方也門
治補下上以制即急制也不緩厭頻而頻多類是而也為偶○一下也門
○物而以為二三方為偶制方也如即通二聖散五八也類是也為偶○也君
複方三下即物合而二為方一方也即如通二聖散五八類也
君二臣一方即偶二之臣三也君一臣三佐五之制也寺君之中也偶也君
六制不偶二之臣四之制偶之小也大也一臣一。○近者三奇之也寺君之二制也偶也君
君制以以下之制也故日制也去也大也君一二一。○汗也臣也君
之調以以詿奇下則者奇氣不味以畢緩補則上微治以以遠制者也寺偶之二制也君
之君一也臣曰佐九制之大也也遠偶古奇之複大方其補也至此治汗也臣
translation:
Seven Formulas

[The text describes the classical Chinese medical theory of the "Seven Formulas" (七方), which categorizes prescriptions into seven types:]

Those [pills] that are taken are easy to transform; refined honey-pills, when taken rotationally, achieve their effect gradually.
Aqueous preparations (decoctions/tang) are given to clear and disperse; pills are for chronic conditions that are difficult to treat — taken gradually, in powder or scattered form, administered rotationally.
Decoctions work by being gradual and moderate; they cannot quickly expel disease; their use is to achieve a slow, thorough effect.
The meaning of this is as follows: large and small refer to the pace — urgent or gradual. Sealed cinnabar preparations are gradual. Pills are again easy to transform and dissolve when refined with honey.

The Seven Formulas: A formula with one ruler (chief herb) and two ministers — this is the large formula. A formula with three ingredients combined into a small formula. A formula with one ruler and two ministers is the supplementing-downward formula.

Regarding the Seven Formulas and nine preparations: large and small refer to urgency and gradualism. A formula with one ruler and two ministers for gradual action; if not large, it is an odd-numbered formula. Gradual without excessive frequency — a formula with one ruler and two ministers is a compound formula; a small formula.

Supplementing downward and upward in regulation — urgent regulation; not gradual, not excessive in frequency; for multiple types of conditions; even-numbered formulas.

Compound formulas: three downward, combining substances together, two forming one formula — just like the Two Sages Powder, five-to-eight types, even-numbered formulas.

A formula with two rulers and one minister is an even pair; three ministers. A formula with one ruler, three ministers, and five assistants is a regulated formula.

Six regulations, not paired — two ministers, four regulations, paired, small, large — one minister to one.

The ruler-formula uses the descending regulation; hence it is called "regulated"; removing the large; one ruler, two, one.

Adjustment uses the strange (odd) and the lower; the strange force, unflavored, gradually supplementing, ascending mildly; treating with distant regulation using even-paired two-regulation formulas.

One ruler, one minister, assistant — nine regulations of the large; distant even-paired ancient odd-numbered compound large formulas; their supplementation reaches this treatment.

text:
十二劑

湯液藥有宜通補瀉輕重滑澀燥濕十劑之法而本經都不言宜之重其後滲濕亦是補劑去之屬即是薑朮燥重大可去之法屬即是牡蠣龍骨可去之濕屬

通湯可藥去有宜通補而本經都不言輕宜之後滲亦去之屬即是麻黃泄可去之法屬即是薑朮防己可去之弱屬即是人也

參羊肉之藥即是麻黃泄可去之法屬即是薑朮防己可去之弱屬即是人也

是磁石輕粉可去之著即是冬葵榆皮之屬即是牡蠣龍骨可去之濕屬

九使此九速如而雞頭制空大心其沸湯服也下去人消亦烯濕未此迷十逐者令是調之合大

九治車○陰前虛酸滅寒平肝下黃多拓用柴水煎為君知頓服佐而以此制之龍膽制吐以苦小寒其神服九之澤服

瀉也如炒米上停○此消制緩緩九也飲子為時時以砭急急不則厭其頻服頑

取其標上壤○留此消制緩緩九也飲子為時時以砭急急不則厭其頻服頑

其少小則治主以緩緩則九之治心其本位近治近客湯以急散不厭其頻服頑

而也多○君臣數一少則二之小腎也肝位遠服湯散不厭其頻服頑

也大則數少少則二之小腎也肝位遠服湯散不厭其頻服頑
translation:
The Twelve Formulas

In herbal medicine, there is the method of the Ten Formulas: those that are appropriate (宜), those that unblock (通), those that tonify (補), those that drain (瀉), those that are light (輕), those that are heavy (重), those that are slippery (滑), those that are astringent (澀), those that dry (燥), and those that are dampening (濕). The original classic does not discuss the "appropriate" category explicitly. The later category of percolating dampness also belongs to the tonifying formulas. Belonging to the drying category are things like ginger and atractylodes. Belonging to the heavy category are things like oyster shell and dragon bone, which can eliminate dampness.

In the unblocking formulas, the appropriate medicines are those that unblock. The original classic does not discuss the light category explicitly. The later percolating category is also a subcategory. Belonging here are things like ephedra, which drains. Belonging to the method of elimination are ginger, atractylodes, and stephania. Belonging to the weakening category is the human component.

Ginseng and mutton are medicines; ephedra belongs to the draining category and can eliminate; ginger, atractylodes, and stephania belong to the elimination method; the weakening subcategory belongs to the human element.

Magnetite and light powder can eliminate; winter mallow and elm bark belong here; oyster shell and dragon bone can eliminate dampness.

For the nine messenger herbs, they act quickly; preparations like chicken-head grain are controlled; large-dose heart-warming decoctions should be boiled and taken; excess moisture should be dried out; the ten expelling agents drive out and regulate, combining into a large formula.

For treating with nine herbs: use decoctions and pills; for conditions of yin deficiency and acid regurgitation with cold and flat sensations in the liver and lower regions, use huang (yellow herbs), add bupleurum, decoct in water, with the chief herb known; take by sips; with gentian to control vomiting; for bitter cold conditions, take nine doses; replenish the essence.

Take the superficial symptoms first; stop here; then reduce and gradually ease; take the nine pills; drink the decoction; use acupuncture when urgent; do not be averse to frequent dosing for stubborn conditions.

For the few versus the many: when there are few sovereign and minister herbs, use gradual and mild approaches; treat the heart at its root; for nearby conditions treat locally; for guest-type disorders use decoctions urgently and frequently; do not be averse to frequent doses for stubborn conditions.

For large versus small dosing: when the formula is large, use fewer doses; when small, use two doses; for the minor kidney and liver conditions, use distant administration via decoctions and powders; do not be averse to frequent dosing for stubborn conditions.

text:
斤兩升斗

皆以盡熟可獨去寒即附子宮桂之熟屬是大也寒補此二種是

即桑白皮赤小豆屬是也溫可去拘即紫石英寒熟屬是也今村補稍此二種是熟屬推寒

二種英何獨寒遺也今許補稍此推屬寒熟

之離鋌有古鋌六稱惟為一鋌分四兩四分無名一名今以六兩十以兩十為泰一鋌云鋌從泰之一分也鋌二也今已正兩云閣鋌依此者此六用仟一

之方泰兩之銅從均之一兩十六兩十為泰一為仟一

今令之即一兩二半也二兩二分之一兩十六兩十

兩銖者為同一今令之即一兩二半也者十以即四今令鋌不久同

九○如泰同一契今令之即日數乃云半主積六小十以成十四兩大今令之一十六一半也者此六用仟一銖為一鍰為一

兩鋌是為二文十六大為一鍰為一銖為偽也兩八為鍰泰為一日十一銖為鍰為一

說累文六○十四鋌為鋌監鋌四八兩為錢兩十四成大故兩十八玉粉泰九元三十日銖半也

四兩四即云水鋌一也升十今為鋌都偽也兩三八銖為鋌泰為一鍰為鍰為一

水○丹淺心法奉命丹銅錄約一計字古今醫鑑化生

斛也即今為之一斤大介之收百一斤今醫鑑錄化微生此用十一
translation:
Weights and Measures: Jin (斤), Liang (兩), Sheng (升), Dou (斗)

All medicines should be fully processed (熟). It is permissible to use alone. Remove coldness. That is, Aconite (附子), Cinnamon Bark (宮桂) — these belong to the warm/hot category. Cold medicines can remove stagnation; that is, Amethyst (紫石英) and cold-natured herbs belong to this category. In contemporary village practice, these are supplemented accordingly. These two categories belong to warm-heat and cold natures.

Regarding the two types: Mulberry root bark (桑白皮) and Red Adzuki Bean (赤小豆) belong to the warm category. How can cold herbs be left out? Today's practitioners supplement these accordingly. These also belong to the cold-heat distinction.

Concerning ancient weight units: An ancient "ting" (鋌) equals six "cheng" (稱). Only one ting is divided into four liang and four fen. Today, six liang equals ten liang, which equals one "tai" (泰). One ting is derived from one fen of tai. This refers to one-twelfth of a liang.

Regarding the copper-based weight standard: one liang equals sixteen zhu (銖); ten liang equals one tai; one qian (千) equals one.

Today's standard: one liang equals two and a half [smaller units]; two liang equals one-half of two fen; ten liang equals sixteen.

Old and new weight comparisons: One huan (鍰) equals one zhu (銖); two wen (文) equals sixteen; one large unit equals one huan, one zhu, or a counterfeit weight; eight liang equals one huan.

Explanatory notes on accumulated weights: Six, ten, fourteen ting equal one jian (監); four, eight liang equal one qian; ten, fourteen equal large standard weights; eighteen equal yupfen (玉粉); nine yuan; thirty days; half a zhu.

Regarding the dan (丹) and measurements of water, sheng, and jin: One modern jin equals the old large standard jin. According to the medical encyclopedia (醫鑑), these have been in use.

text:
煮藥法

為上取水清量病者為人之煎藥必擇器煎熟制度令親誠至意

馬虎人為之煎藥也少無耐不以除油慢火煎煎必用薪絲甘水

也六大鉢若是愚四令之分之紹一興耳牛中九言二升牛若用二合之半則

六升也六升二分當令之一門四○錢七沈牛存一四當鍾有讓四一字宇四○分九云一錢字也

即十二二分鉢半鉢三二一四錢二有分四一宇○六九云二一錢半字也

十四分即為鉢二半也五三銅一二分乃半知一一六字為二一分半也

无即此方其銅鑰一二分乃半知一六字為二一分半也

煎乾八石渣分器汁水煎七可不以拒域表汗下煎至之藥分藥法用

煎或至一八盞煎至八分○補藥至利藥一盞半生去補藥服後留水再煎極至銅至

乾亦不對微病者熱煎至七可太浚補表汗下煎至大藥分不服煎用須絲甘水

分可補湯火煎驗熬乾至分太浚補表汗之煎至藥分服可煎至極至銅至金大

盈煎或至一八盞煎至八分○補藥利藥欲熟多水而小取一
translation:
Method of Decocting Medicine

When preparing medicine, first take a measured amount of clean water appropriate to the patient's condition. When decocting medicine for a person, one must choose the proper vessel, control the heat, and bring the medicine to a proper boil, doing so with sincerity and full attention.

If the task is left carelessly to an inattentive person, there will be insufficient patience and the oil will not be removed; slow fire decoction is required. Only clean water and fine silk-strained water should be used.

[Measurements and proportions for various vessel sizes and decoction amounts follow, specifying cups, ounces, and portions.]

For drying decoctions: when using stone vessels, remove the dregs, measure the juice and water. Decoct until reduced. Do not let it become too condensed. Sweating-inducing and purgative medicines should be decocted to a full cup; tonic medicines should be decocted to one and a half cups. The dregs may be re-decocted with water and taken again.

For dry preparations: similarly adjust the amount of water according to whether the medicine is a tonic, a diaphoretic, or a purgative. Decoct until reduced to the appropriate fraction. For tonic medicines requiring much water, take a small amount at a time.

text:
服藥法

加計濁藥煎欲生少水而多取汁以大棗治發散至高寒之病

蔥白去濕去以藥上五錢水○若發散而服用一二沸一服水

少者今當藥只以藥五錢水○古方半用作一而服用水

燒傷後○主病藥宜先煎眼如發汗則先煎麻黃去一二沸

然傷後八主病藥同宜先煎眼止發汗先煎麻黃一二沸

胡濕傷風八先煎薑防風木風無毒服暑固此先煎香桂枝和解先煎柴胡黃

需黃方有市大日小有毒無毒服固而約以煎先煎香桂枝和解先煎柴黃

無去毒其病六治不正也○若九十裁去毒肉果七常食養病之毒無去八

之止傷其毒治六病常去也○若九十裁去肉果七常食養盧病之使過

藥智而購以止食之不宜去病後以悟鈍病之之之先走盧虛度

煎者宜飽病者在四肢血後去用藥病為腹病先

清者宜飢病在在空腹以下補於下

骨髓宜急飲食緩在上

服宜多服則滋補藥在上多服則峻而為地煎

武服骨宜急飲食緩綏在上○不宜多服則滋補藥在上多服則峻補於下下壞○大傾九而濃
translation:
Methods for Taking Medicine

When decocting medicines such as Jia-ji-zhuo (complex decoctions), one should simmer them to reduce the liquid and concentrate the juice. Use a large jujube to treat dispersing conditions. For high-level cold diseases, use scallion whites to dispel dampness. Use five qian of medicine to one measure of water. For dispersing formulas, bring to one or two boils and take in one dose with water.

For those with deficiency, the current standard is to use five qian of medicine with water. According to the old formula, use half that amount, prepare once, and take with water in one or two boilings.

For burn injuries: the primary medicinal should first be decocted; for eye conditions involving sweating, first decoct ephedra until one or two boils have occurred.

For wind-damp injuries, first decoct ginger and saposhnikovia root. For wood-wind conditions that are non-toxic, for summerheat disorders, first decoct cinnamon twig and harmonizing medicines; first decoct bupleurum and scutellaria.

For toxic and non-toxic medicines: use approximately this method of decocting first.

Regarding the timing of medicine intake: if there is damage from toxic substances, treat it by removing the toxin from the flesh and fruit. For nourishing the body after illness, do not take too much; after illness, the mind may become dulled.

The wise physician instructs the patient to eat beforehand; for conditions in the four limbs and blood, use medicine after removing pathology; for abdominal conditions, treat the abdomen first.

Clear medicines should be taken on an empty stomach; for conditions in the lower body, nourish from below.

For bone marrow conditions, take urgently with food; for upper-body conditions, a gradual approach with food is appropriate.

Regarding dosage: for more doses, use tonic medicines for upper-body conditions; for concentrated lower-body decoctions, take in larger amounts. For drastic tonification of the lower body, do not take excessively. Large doses should be taken nine times in a concentrated form.

text:
玉味藥

服藥寒熱飲熱藥寒欲中和之劑溫而服之雖補腎之藥難納

○服藥陽藥須令熱服陰藥須令冷服初一言而下冷語下不可太急人也五門要初吐補腎之藥難納

開綃時言萬語嚥唾功敗氣印合當碯磁膺而生龍吟得漆而漆麻得而漆雲而起

藥性共藥桂毛羽之屬得蔥而軟韌性得樹柏性而桔累不剿而覆思分之蓋而漆龍

其謂於以法世青而頻桔我苦不剿得腥而漆思分之蓋而漆龍吟得漆而漆麻

丹砂法火故色赤陽而生以此陽世法木故色鮮青介之主頻桔我苦不剿得腥而漆

生妨雛黃法土故色黃而主心脾雲而法金故色白而主肺法水故色黑而對淡曰

肺主發散○丹法為黃帝色赤陽而生故色陰而主砒磁法妨黑味何伯對淡日

辛味或奧或世甘腎或世為陽或收澀為陰或行或調其氣味合而服之以養五為以補

果辛為助五畜為益五菜為充氣味合而服之以補精益氣五穀為養五果為助五畜為益五菜為充氣味合而服之以補精益氣
translation:
Five Flavors of Medicines

When taking medicines, if it is a cold medicine, drink it warm; if it is a hot medicine, take it cold — this seeks a balanced, harmonious preparation. Even tonifying kidney medicines can be difficult to swallow if taken improperly.

Regarding yang medicines: they must be taken hot. Regarding yin medicines: they must be taken cold. Initially one speaks of taking them down with cold liquid, but one must not rush too hastily. There are five key principles. If taken improperly, even tonifying kidney medicines will be hard to receive.

On the properties of medicines: Medicines such as cinnamon bark belong to the category of feathers and fur — they soften when combined with scallions and become pliable; the nature of cypress and platycodon, when combined, can be counteracted when combined with lacquer and hemp.

On the colors of medicines: Cinnabar corresponds to fire, so its color is red, belonging to yang, governing the heart. It corresponds to wood, so its color is green, governing the liver. Yellow orpiment corresponds to earth, so its color is yellow, governing the spleen and stomach. White medicines correspond to metal, so their color is white, governing the lungs. Black medicines correspond to water, so their color is black, governing the kidneys.

The five flavors — acrid, sweet, sour, bitter, salty — each have their yin and yang aspects: some are dispersing, some are astringent, some promote movement, some harmonize. When their qi and flavors are combined and taken together, they nourish the five organs.

The five grains nourish; the five fruits assist; the five meats benefit; the five vegetables supplement. When their qi and flavors are combined and taken together, they replenish the essence and boost the qi.

text:
收益氣此五者有辛酸甘苦鹹各時四藏所利或散或收或緩或急或堅或軟鹹鹹味酸甘苦鹹各時五藏病隨宜制五味宮五味或散或收
為或五也緩味過則五。味者之維口生咀嚼兩而欲本食在五五必辛先冬各歸制五宮
所使在宜五也酸過則先入傷其者之也正也也入鹹而夫五味入五辛先入胃自各制五宮
則先喜過攻焉酸過則先入傷肝其正也也入口生咀而夫五味入五辛先冬各歸
也鹹先入酸過則先入絕腎益多而且比益藏物年化心。甘先入五辛先冬各歸制
也。入絕腎益多而少比益藏常氣偏增兩腑氣久有大五而偏之入肺其由
大則也絕藏有由偷則不暴亦大亡天斯考鼓日由氣勝兩氣久有無而入肺由
味偏則絕其不有暴亦大亡天斯考鼓日氣勝両氣久有大五而偏
由傷能也有餘合服飯偏絕則不暴亦大亡天考鼓散氣勝両氣久
結益助也能爆燥散有偏絕則不暴亦大亡天散氣由
炸苦此能能爆燥結合服飯軟食酸能亦暴大散
味大則軟坚淡能爆燥結合服飯軟食酸能
也润软坚谈能甘能利窠球软坚酸能亦
酸滋润软坚谈甘利窠直下用散收甘。辛
能止而軟堅談甘利窠直下用散收欲能緩散而
酸止能表裹而藥能氣上利甘行窠直下而用
表裹而止。數藥本氣上利甘行窠直下而酸
謂火渗表裹而止。數藥本氣小也酸上升鹹收而甘
過數火熟滲也其内暨其本氣小也酸升鹹收而甘
蘇大也骨氣。謂瀉小便上升鹹收甘其結大之辛淡以滲其裨補骸廢散之辛辛
過蘇大也骨氣。勞短肌心兼肝氣以澤蘇謂乃絕末大之辛淡以滲其裨補骸廢散散
translation:
The five flavors — pungent, sour, sweet, bitter, and salty — each have their appropriate seasons and their relationships to the five viscera. They may disperse, astringe, moderate, firm, or soften. The salty flavor, the sour, sweet, bitter, and salty each correspond to the seasons and to diseases of the five viscera; one should use the five flavors appropriately according to the illness, governing the five palaces of the body.

Excess of the sour flavor first enters and damages the liver; its proper function is to enter through the mouth. The five flavors enter the five viscera, with pungent first entering in winter, each returning to govern its palace.

If salty is taken in excess, it first enters and injures the kidneys, accumulating and causing imbalance; this increases the visceral qi and over time creates bias and damage to the organs.

Excess use leads to depletion of the stored essence; the qi becomes weakened over time, imbalanced in the viscera and bowels, and through prolonged use the lung is affected.

When flavors are used in excess, depletion of the stored essence results, leading to sudden damage, wasting, and deterioration — this is how the qi is defeated.

Sourness can astringe and moisten; it softens hardness. Sweetness can moderate and harmonize, facilitate movement downward, and disperse. Bitterness can dry and firm; it can consolidate and help food be digested. Pungency can scatter and disperse; it can move upward and promote circulation. Saltiness can soften hardness and guide things downward.

Bitterness firms and dries. Pungency disperses and moves outward through the surface and interior, stopping accumulation and benefiting the qi upward. Sweetness moves through the channels, nourishing and supplementing, moderating and warming. These are the fundamental natures of the five flavors governing the bones, muscles, and visceral qi, regulating the small intestines, promoting rising and astringing, and nourishing the body throughout.

text:
氣味升降

○ 滿色黒。乃主腎氣。不衝味。過於苦。胛意不瀉。胃氣乃尊。

○ 正王味辛。不敵以疏。腠膜酝理。精神乃欲。

類多蔬。乃則傷肝。行自戰偷。則傷多故。心以多則傷脾。苦多則長有天。肺氣辛納。腎脊尊。

眼蒙蒙辣苦。吐氣亦朱。彼多則傷心。此五味。辣辣者蒜辣。心薑辣。五味辛刻脊。

○ 陽為氣。陰為味。味出下竅。氣出上竅。清之薄者。陽中之陰。清之厚者。純陽。薄則發泄。厚則發熱。濁之薄者。陰中之陽。濁之厚者。純陰。薄則通。厚則滋。

○ 清陽發腠理。濁陰出膜理。清陽實四肢。濁陰歸六府。清陽發上竅。濁陰走下竅。

味薄者為陰中之陽。味厚者為純陰。氣薄者為陽中之陰。氣厚者為純陽。

○ 辛甘淡薄者為陽。酸苦鹹味為陰。

陽浮。故味薄者為陽。下走。故藏熱為陽。清之薄上。則發泄。清之厚者純陽。氣薄則陰者為之純陽。氣厚。味上則清陽。氣發腠膜理。

陽故瀉。下走。故味薄者為陽中之陰。陰浮。薄者為陰純氣也。味厚則陰通世利。薄則炎上。故氣薄則泄熱。謂天汗之味薄潤。

也為下。故陰涼。寒者。天之陰也。陽溫。陽炎上。止故氣薄則泄熱。謂天汗之出薄陰純氣涸。門。或味陰之有。

陽也。訒陰少。故通世利。薄則炎。氣薄者為陽中之陰也。溫涼寒熱。是也。厚則發熱。則謂熱味薄者。天之出薄陰純氣也。
translation:
Rising and Descending of Qi and Flavor

○ When the color is full and dark, this governs Kidney Qi. If the flavor is not balanced and is excessively bitter, the spleen and stomach's intent becomes impaired, yet Stomach Qi remains sovereign.

○ The proper governing flavor is pungent. When not counterbalanced, it opens and disperses the interstices and membranes, allowing the spirit and essence to thrive.

Among the various flavors: if sour is excessive it damages the Liver; if salty is excessive it damages the Heart; if sweet is excessive it damages the Spleen; if bitter is excessive it may benefit the Lungs; pungent flavors enter the Kidneys. These proportions determine health.

Among pungent and bitter tastes: garlic is pungently hot, ginger is hot. All five flavors when excessive harm the corresponding organs.

○ Yang is Qi; Yin is Flavor. Flavor exits through the lower orifices; Qi exits through the upper orifices. The clear and thin is Yin within Yang. The clear and thick is pure Yang. The thin disperses and vents outward; the thick generates heat. The turbid and thin is Yang within Yin; the turbid and thick is pure Yin. The thin opens passages; the thick nourishes and enriches.

○ Clear Yang opens the interstices; Turbid Yin exits through the membranes. Clear Yang fills the four limbs; Turbid Yin returns to the six bowels. Clear Yang rises to the upper orifices; Turbid Yin descends to the lower orifices.

Thin-flavored substances are Yin within Yang. Thick-flavored substances are pure Yin. Thin-Qi substances are Yin within Yang. Thick-Qi substances are pure Yang.

○ Pungent, sweet, and bland flavors belong to Yang. Sour, bitter, and salty flavors belong to Yin.

Yang floats upward; therefore thin-flavored substances belong to Yang. Descending action is also associated with Yang when warmth is stored. Clear thin substances rise and vent outward; thick clear substances are pure Yang. When Qi is thin and Yin, together they form pure Yang. With thick Qi and clear-rising flavor, Yang Qi opens the interstices.

When Yang is dispersed downward, thin-flavored substances belong to Yin within Yang. When Yin floats, thin substances become pure Yin in terms of Qi. Thick flavor enables Yin to flow through, while thin substances flare upward; thus thin Qi vents heat — this is what is meant by thin flavor and perspiration moistening.

Being of a descending nature, Yin is cool. Cold belongs to the Yin of Heaven; warmth and Yang flare upward. Hence thin Qi vents heat. The meaning of perspiration arising from thin Yin is that pure Yin Qi becomes exhausted. Whether flavor is Yin depends on circumstance.

Yang pertains to Yin in its restraining aspect, with little Yin; it therefore flows through and is beneficial. The thin flares up; thin Qi is thus Yin within Yang. Warm, cool, cold, and hot — these are examples. The thick generates heat, and thick-flavored substances that are heat-generating are called such because they are thin-flavored in terms of pure Yin Qi.

translation:
This is a passage from classical Chinese medicine theory, dealing with the properties of medicinal substances according to the Yin-Yang and Qi-flavor framework:

Flavor is the image of taste. Sweet and bland, fine and thin, belong to the yang aspect of earth. Sour and bitter belong to the yin of heaven. Salty belongs to the yin of earth. When flavor is thin, it is light and clear. Pungent and bland thin flavors belong to the category of earth, and through the root they connect to sourness. Bitter, salty, and hot belong to the ground. Flavor that is thick and salty, hot, bitter, sweet, cold, or warm — this is flavor in its fullness. Thin flavor belongs to yin within yang; when flavor is thick it promotes discharge. Pungent, sweet, bland, and neutral flavors, when the qi is thin, allow passage through. Sour, bitter, and salty cold flavors represent the thickness of yin. Thin flavors belong to yang within yin. When qi is thin it moves through. Yin within yang — when flavor is thick, the herbs of the Materia Medica do not speak of "bland" as a separate flavor, yet neutral is also present.

Cold, hot, cold — the same region belongs to yang among the five. When qi is thin it promotes bitterness; when flavor is thick it calms and clears, rising subtly. Cold herbs also ascend, clearing and separating. Nourishing through the ying (nutritive qi) to assist the descent, clearing the yang, truly — this is clearing. Yang among the five, thin qi, clearing and calming — clearing within turbid, steaming and clearing within.

Category: Wind — Ascending — Generating
[Herbs:] Psyllium seed (粘子), Atractylodes (蒼朮), Hemp (麻黄), Schizonepeta (荊芥), Peppermint (薄荷), Peucedanum (前胡), Gentian root (秦艽) — [these promote] thick discharge. Platycodon (桔梗), Cimicifuga (升麻), Siler (防風).

Category: Heat — Floating — Growing
[Herbs:] Dried ginger — those that are thick and generating are good. Galangal (良薑), Cinnamon bark (肉桂), Cinnamon twig (桂枝), Grass cardamom (草豆蔻), Cloves (丁香), Magnolia bark (厚朴), Aconite (烏頭).

Method for Using Root and Branch (梢) Portions:
Medicinal plants are divided according to where they grow: parts underground (roots), parts at mid-level, and upper portions (branches/tips). For diseases in the upper body (head and upper burner), use the upper portions of the herb; for diseases in the middle of the body (middle burner), use the middle sections; for diseases in the lower body (lower burner), use the root portion. For the lower extremities, use the lower root portions. The body is divided into upper, middle, and lower sections, and correspondingly, the herb is divided into tip (梢), middle, and root, each applied to the matching bodily region. When cutting, slice with a knife according to these categories.

translation:
Tonifying and Draining the Five Viscera

On the correspondence of form to function. The throat. Angelica root returns to the head, stops bleeding, and moves upward through the body; below it nourishes the blood and guards the center; it cuts off fire from below.

To suppress is to drain by suppression. Quite substantially. Fire also follows this principle. Ledebouriella (Fangfeng) is preventive. Tonify the mother organ; if there is excess, drain the child organ. For example, if the liver is excessive, drain the heart, because the heart is the child of the liver. Cold drains the heart. Tonify the spleen and drain the heart, because the spleen is the mother of the heart. ○ If the spleen needs draining, tonify the heart. When one should tonify, cold-natured herbs drain. ○ Qi-warming herbs tonify; cold herbs drain the Gate of Life. Together with the heart and small intestine.

When both organs are excessive: the heart is protected. One should tonify the liver and gallbladder. Sweet flavor tonifies the liver; bitter drains it; acrid tonifies; sour drains. ○ Warming qi tonifies the Gate of Life and large intestine; vermilion (Zhu) sour tonifies; salty tonifies.

Spleen: drain with green-natured herbs; sweet flavor tonifies; bitter drains; acrid warm and hot herbs drain; cold herbs refine and tonify qi; sweet-bitter warm herbs drain the kidneys and bladder; Zhu bitter tonifies; salty drains; lungs and large intestine drain; Zhu sour together tonifies.

Heart: use warm Zhu (cinnabar-processed), cooked, to drain in cases of heat. Household sweet herbs tonify and drain warmth; supplement with salty herbs. In this domain: Evodia fruit, Cinnamon bark, Atractylodes, White Atractylodes, Acorus root, Coptis.

Zhao method: use Polygala, Cornu [deer horn], return to Cnidium and Peony. Yellow: Cow bezoar, Bamboo leaves, Cinnabar, Ophiopogon, Acorus, Coptis.

Tonify with salt. Drain with Coptis, Sophora root, Fritillaria, Peucedanum, Ophiopogon, Alpinia, Gold. Gastrodia, Ophiopogon, Cuscuta, Ginseng, Gold foil, stir-fried.

Small Intestine: household, warm nature, use Peony, Phellodendron, Akebia, Scutellaria, Trichosanthes powder, Talcum, Plantain seed.

translation:
This page from the Dongui Bogam (Herbal Medicine section) describes the guiding medicinal herbs (引經藥) for various organ meridians and their associated treatment principles. The content outlines which herbs guide medicinal action to specific organs and channels:

For the Lung meridian: use Platycodon (桔梗), Baibu, and Shengma (升麻) as guiding herbs; for lesser ailments use Baishao (白芍).

For the Stomach meridian: use Gegen (葛根, kudzu root) and Baibu as guiding herbs; Huangqi and Shengma also guide upward.

For the Large Intestine meridian: use Baishao (白芍) and Shengma as guiding herbs.

For the Heart meridian and Pericardium: use Huanglian and Danzhu as guiding herbs; Fuzi (附子, aconite) guides to the lesser channels.

For the Kidney meridian: use Duhuo (獨活) and Zhimu (知母) as guiding guides; wine-prepared herbs also guide there.

For the Spleen meridian: use Gegen and Baishao; Cangzhu also treats dampness-related conditions.

General rules: For heat in the limbs and joint pain, use Gegen and Huangqin. For deficiency conditions, use Guizhi (桂枝) and Gegen. For phlegm-dampness, use Banxia (半夏) and Chenpi (陳皮). For stagnation, use Zhishi (枳實) and Houpo (厚朴). For cold conditions, add warming herbs. Chuanxiong (川芎) guides to the head region; Chaihu (柴胡) guides to the lesser yang channel. Qianghuo (羌活) and Duhuo guide to the upper and lower body respectively.

translation:
Dietary Prohibitions When Taking Medicine

Atractylodes macrocephala (白术/蒼术): To regulate qi, one must use aucklandia root (木香). To supplement qi, one must use ginseng (人參) where there is fire constitution. To harmonize the blood, one must use wine-washed blood-moving herbs.

To address upper burner conditions, one must use prepared coptis (黃連). One must use anemarrhena (知母), prepared phellodendron (黃柏), alisma (澤瀉), and poria (茯苓).

For qi stagnation in the middle, one must use citrus peel (青皮), sliced phellodendron (黃柏), dry poria (茯苓), stir-fried poria, and coptis to eliminate dampness.

For rib-region qi stagnation, one must use aurantium (枳殼), and for food stagnation and distension, use aurantium, atractylodes, and poria; for itching sores use Baoyu formula.

For fullness and pain in the abdomen, use licorice (甘草) and rhubarb (大黃). For bladder issues, for lower abdominal pain and bloating, use cardamom (草豆蔲) and tangerine peel (青皮) and alisma.

For cold in the abdomen, use licorice and mirabilite (芒硝).

For conditions requiring pure preparation, use phellodendron.

When using pure preparations, one must harmonize with licorice and combine accordingly.

For conditions of cold and heat, certain medicinal sliding/lubricating substances may be eaten, but this must be adjusted carefully with herbal preparations.

Strong pure preparations may be taken with medicines, but one should not eat too many spicy or raw vegetables.

Fatty intestines and similar substances should not be eaten in large amounts while taking medicine; one must avoid wearing soiled clothing.

Oily, greasy, and cured meats and similar items must not be combined with fattening herbs and raw foods.

One must generally avoid the intake of grains that are overly refined and fattening.

Prohibited items include: salted fish, fresh fish, pinellia (半夏), acorus (菖蒲); do not eat maltose, taro, sparrow meat, clams, seaweed, green onions, spinach, garlic, or any dish containing garlic.

translation:
This page contains classical Chinese medical text discussing dietary prohibitions and incompatibilities with various herbal medicines. The content covers:

Ground rehmannia (地黄) and Polygonum multiflorum (何首烏): Do not eat green onions, garlic, chives, or radishes when taking these medicines.

Coptis (黄連): Do not eat pork or pork products when taking this herb. This prohibition applies for up to three years. Also incompatible with細辛 (Asarum).

Sesame (胡麻): Avoid eating radishes.

Various other herbs have their own dietary restrictions listed, including prohibitions against eating certain fish, meats, vinegar, vegetables, and other foods when taking specific medicines.

The text follows the traditional Chinese medical format of listing each medicinal substance followed by foods and substances that must be avoided while taking that medicine, as these combinations were believed to cause harm or reduce the medicine's effectiveness.

text:
忌銅鐵藥

肉忌。龍骨忌魚。肉忌。香蒜忌。杏仁食大蒜。米忌破故紙忌蔥忌羊。肉忌。蜜忌食蔥及羊。耳忌食蔗恒。諸藥忌食恒。能制諸毒之藥。本草甲高草。膳甘忌地黃。白解毒梅草。苗食忌恒。一白角忌大白地黃。九鹿綠藥忌。切蒸肝氣忌惡。器而何惡之也日。者無燃以自伐地爛。銅鉄柴以白銅皮。補掘氣鐵者。無以銅肉補其又。肾桑說覺何他。忌有寄生彼。消用刀銅銀以白鉄。刀竹宜篏以白石銀男銅刀損。煎石鍋令忌竹銅。削刀以用銅。銀鋃竹刀令。以銅鐵鍋刀忌竹。箬令之以鐵切若銅。忌用鉄鋃以鉄鍋。铁刀令玄根以鋃。参勿用銅鐵鋃刀削刀。皮棟令宜以用人。竹以銅銀刀刀。宜篏令竹消通升生。忌者白鐵柴。令男以白石。銅鍋刀損以銅。刀磨以令磁皮或竹。磁器竹木切刀忌銅鉄。切竹葉根。刀匙勿切香。附鉄子与石鉄。铁以白中銅。壯刀削令皮棟。玄根以鋃参勿。用令之石鉄忌竹。鐵飯之壺人鐵。与人銭目以銅中壯刀削令玄根以鋃参勿用銅鐵鍋刀削刀以鐵切若銅。磁器竹木。刀尺母令盆地黄不可近令犯桑枝也。草母犯鐵器。同令令人。肾补他桑说。覺其仲子陽忌有。蒸其者補鐵鍋器。無以銅補其又。鉄齐也黄。類銅。見九鹿之銅切藥黃得。地不黄九。藥之铁柘其。柘黃也。補腎其姝令母犯桑虛。近之可不令同。肝補可以地之黃不子令母犯。盆地黄不可以宜竹鍛令男以用人木虛令者柘補腎令母犯桑虛其仲子陽忌蒸。草著名。食者必齋耳者。蒴花力盖蒙药九鹿。菀蒿名食必不。得萬藥肉。救青豬恒食忌解毒梅草。苗食恒。

草蒼耳齊。九鹿一白角。大白地黃。高草能。本草甲制諸毒之藥。諸藥忌食蔗恒。耳忌食蔗恒。肉忌蜜忌食蔥及羊。
translation:
Herbs Incompatible with Copper and Iron

Dragon bone is incompatible with fish meat. Garlic is incompatible with almonds when eaten together. Broken papaya seeds are incompatible with scallions and mutton. Honey is incompatible with scallions and lamb's ear. Various medicines are incompatible with constant consumption of sugarcane. Medicines that can counteract various poisons: according to the Materia Medica, Gao herb (mugwort group), Shan Gan is incompatible with rehmannia. White plum can detoxify. Seedlings and shoots should not be consumed constantly.

Regarding copper and iron: many herbal preparations must not come into contact with copper or iron vessels. When decocting medicines, one should use stone pots, bamboo utensils, or wooden implements. Copper and iron pots, ladles, and knives are to be avoided. If bamboo, wooden, or ceramic vessels are used instead, the medicinal properties are preserved. Iron and copper cookware can corrupt the nature of certain herbs, particularly rehmannia (Dihuang), which must not be cooked near copper implements or mulberry branches.

The kidneys are supplemented by certain herbs, but these must not be brought near mulberry wood or iron vessels. When processing these medicines, stone or ceramic tools are preferred.

Herbs such as Cang Er (cocklebur), nine-deer herb, white-horned herb, rehmannia, and Gao herb are capable of counteracting various poisons. Various medicines are incompatible with constant sugarcane consumption. Honey must not be taken together with scallions and mutton.

translation:
Mutually Incompatible Medicines (Xiang Fan Yao)

This section describes medicinal substances that are incompatible with iron, copper, or other metals during preparation, as well as those that are mutually antagonistic when combined.

Regarding iron utensils: Many medicines must not come into contact with iron. When processing, use a copper knife to scrape away the skin and bones. Dragon bone (Long Gu) must not touch iron. Winter preparations using iron are also prohibited in certain cases. Bamboo instruments may be used instead.

Regarding copper utensils: Chai Hu (Bupleurum) must avoid copper knives. Certain preparations require iron knives to remove bones and outer skin before use.

Lotus root, peach skin, and similar substances: Use copper knives; avoid iron. For all bone and horn medicines, iron knives are used for scraping.

Concerning the large nine categories [of incompatibilities]:

Regarding mutual antagonism: Realgar (Xiong Huang) and similar substances — these are described as mutually repelling. Dragon bone (Long Gu) and Cattle Gallstone (Niu Huang) are mutually antagonistic. These combinations are called "mutual aversion."

On the incompatibility of Ginseng (Shen Shen): Ginseng is incompatible with Li Lu (Veratrum). Purple-covered varieties and fine Hu (胡) herbs are also mutually incompatible. Black, Xia (summer), and Huang (yellow) varieties — certain combinations must not be mixed or used together.

On arsenic compounds and their antagonists: Arsenic (Pi Shuang), Saltpeter (Xiao), Lacquer (Qi), and related substances — these are mutually incompatible with certain herbs including Aconite head (Wu Tou), Licorice (Gan Cao), Rhinoceros horn (Xi Jiao), and others.

Dolichos bean (Dou), Rhinoceros horn, Ox horn, aromatics — these form groups of seven or more mutual incompatibilities along with arsenic and related mineral substances.

Method of Steeping Medicines
The text states: steep and extract by fumigating over a day's fire. translation:
Well-Flower Water (Jeonghwa Water — the first draw of well water at dawn)

Water drawn from nearby rivers and streams is second in quality. In cities and densely populated areas, well water may be mixed with sewage and become alkaline; if both [qualities are compromised], the well water will later become turbid and cloudy, and one must then boil and grind peach and apricot [kernels] with wine to take it. This is not a direct [remedy but a corrective measure].

Among all drinking waters, this one is appropriate for drinking; it also treats illness. Drawn fresh from a clear spring that is not turbid or cloudy, it should be used [before the water settles and turns muddy]; if it turns turbid, one must boil and grind [remedies] with wine to take.

[Regarding its preparation:] After [the water] is drawn to wash, scrub, and refine, the well water floats and settles. When used in the morning on today's water surface, [the description follows] — it is good for washing the face and eyes, clearing the skin, is non-toxic, and is beneficial to people when taken with alcohol in large quantities.

The names [of methods] and modifications thereof are described: taken as medicine to clear and benefit, to open the throat and the cinnabar [energy field], the scenery is best when used this way. Its good nature and clean taste are like snow water; every day take it to brew and cook until spring.

New water, used in small amounts, added into a red gold decoction; when boiled, it can resolve combined oral toxins and detoxify fish poisoning.

Its qi [energy] is such that when used in small amounts and added to a red gold decoction and boiled, it can be drawn and used for steaming, washing, and bathing. Its nature benefits large and small urination, clears the body, and it can resolve combined oral toxins and detoxify fish poisoning.

Chrysanthemum Flower Water

Long-term consumption prolongs life and prevents aging. It is non-toxic. There is a place where chrysanthemums grow along the cliffs and streams; the people who live there drink this water. Their water source comes from the chrysanthemum gardens of Nanyang County. The people there drink this water and live to two or three hundred years of age without exception. Laba Snow Water (Twelfth Month Snow Water)

[Collected during the twelfth lunar month.] The red flowers and snow are collected. This snow water is cold in nature. The cold qi of the year descends, and in the regular season this cold qi is present. It follows the cold cycle through the year. It treats all manner of toxins, also relieves jaundice and various skin sores and swellings. Taste: sweet, non-toxic.

Spring Rain Water

It promotes the generation of medicinal efficacy. One cup taken invigorates the yang qi. Therefore it can be used to increase yang in those who are deficient. On the first month, the rain water rises with the spring energy. When the spring rain is abundant, husband and wife each separately decoct [their medicines with it].

Autumn Dew Water

Used to make wine, it produces a clear, bright color. It is collected from various plants and stored; it tastes sweet and stops thirst. When consumed, it lightens the body.

Autumn dew collected from the leaves of plants nourishes and moistens the skin. Its nature is balanced and its taste is non-toxic. Morning dew, when applied to the eyes, brightens eyesight. The dew collected in autumn from the tops of many flowers, when gathered and used, brightens the eyes.

Autumn dew water collected from mulberry leaves nourishes the complexion when consumed. Collecting autumn dew water from flower tops improves the appearance. Winter Frost

Ground into a fine powder; when applied to the face it is known to be cooling in nature, non-toxic, and when consumed it mainly resolves intoxication, soothes the aftermath of drinking.

Thunder Water

Absorbed and drawn in, it governs the harmonizing of flavors; gathered and stored properly, it maintains its original qualities and does not spoil over time.

Summer Water

Useful for long-standing ailments; its nature when consumed regularly provides great benefit, supplements vitality, extends life, removes restlessness, and is recommended for use during summer months for refreshing the body.

Various Waters (方諸水 and related entries)

Fanzhū Water (方諸水)
[Collected from the reflection of moonlight on a mirror-like vessel.] It settles the mind and calms restlessness in children, relieves hot irritability and thirst. Its flavor is sweet, non-toxic, and it is particularly effective for brightening [the eyes and mind].

Plum Rain Water (梅雨水)
[Collected during the plum rain season.] It can reduce [stains], and morning dew combined with this water is effective for washing away grime from clothing. Its nature is cold; the juice is effective in the fifth month. It is primarily used for washing and cleansing sores and wounds.

Celestial River Water / Rainwater Collected in High Places (牛天河水)
It can nurture children's spirit and mental vigor. It is suitable for drinking. Along with it, water collected in hollows of tall trees and bamboo tubes—such clear water is good for drinking, and calms madness, evil influences, and pacifies harmful energies.

[Used] to regulate and harmonize [conditions]. Collected from eaves after rain passes through celestial pools, it is used to treat active sores of the head, and the accumulated vapor within bamboo tubes; over time this water can be refined and used medicinally.

Thatched Roof Leak Water (茅屋漏水)
[It is] toxic. Used for bites [from venomous creatures]. One must use the dripping water carefully, letting it flow down and accumulate, then apply to the affected sores and wounds. [Also used in certain external treatments.]

It nourishes and moistens the body. Its nature is neutral, taste sweet, non-toxic. Long-term consumption makes people healthy. Thousand-Li Water (千里水)

It can relieve abdominal fullness when used to decoct medicine. Take water that has flowed far and long. Water that travels along roads through summer and autumn, through various terrain, can be used to decoct medicine for conditions of the limbs. Do not take water that merely flows downhill.

Turbulent Agitated Water (甘爛水)
For treating running pulse disorders and other conditions: the method is to place water in a large basin and ladle it repeatedly to agitate it.

Eddy Water (逆流水)
This refers to water that flows in reverse, i.e., water that eddies back against the current. Flowing Water (順流水)

Rapid Current Water (急流水)

It is used for wind diseases, governing all wind conditions, joint contracture and spasm, skin disorders, knee impediment, and weakness of the hands and feet. All sores and ulcers, including syphilitic sores (yangmei sores), are healed by bathing in it. Because it contains arsenic and alum, it cures wind-cold conditions and various sores.

translation:
Cold Springs (冷泉)

Gruel Water (漿水)

Earth Juice (地漿)

Cool Water (涼水)

Raw and Cooked Broth (生熟湯)

[Cold Springs]
For people who are cold-averse and have symptoms such as those listed: In the seventh and eighth months it is commonly said one should not bathe at night. It thoroughly clears the body. Boiling millet removes turbidity, aids sleep, and dispels drowsiness. The water, once cooked and heated, is best for those who are good candidates — it expels summer heat. It is said to treat cholera and promote bowel regularity. Its flavor is sour and astringent.

[Gruel Water / Leaven Water]
This water can counteract all kinds of poison in humans. Its nature is cold and non-toxic. It can also resolve various toxic conditions. It also resolves maple-tree poisoning. People say it is used in the mountains and that the yellow earth in it [has medicinal use].

[Earth Juice]
Earth juice is made by digging into the ground. Those who cannot eat are given it to drink — it is said that in the mountains, the earth at the center [of a pit] is used. Its nature is non-toxic. It resolves all poisons, including those from the middle of [toxic] remedies, and also resolves maple poisoning.

[Cool Water]
It is also called "添山" water. It is prepared by soaking mountain roots and serving the strained liquid. The flavor is mild. It does not injure by cold, but can cause the eruption of yellow rash. The cool [water with] coptis...

[Raw and Cooked Broth]
This refers to food that supplements and replenishes. It stirs the center and sustains new vitality, so the formula calls for roasting with salt and adding it to the drink. Its flavor is salty and non-toxic. It is used to expel lodged food and toxins from the body. Roast with salt and add to the drink.

汗沿出半熟之則食熟陽病須服之以上湯忽漬脚及至膝學覆

過汗而世舍虛熱呂食之麻沸渴取其氣薄毒故

translation:
Boiled Water (熟湯)

Boiled water is called "ba" water. People drink it plain or with food. When boiling water, use half new water and half previously boiled water steeped until the sharp taste is gone.

One should combine well water and spring water in equal parts, mixing yin and yang together — this preparation is called Yin-Yang Decoction (陰陽湯). It can be used to treat salt poisoning.

It is said to promote the flow of qi, and its nature is balanced. It is also called Sweet Yin-Yang Decoction. In cases of sudden cramping and cholera with spasms reaching from the feet up to the knees, it is effective.

In cases of excessive sweating, when the body is weakened by heat, consuming this half-boiled preparation is beneficial. It is also used for heat disorders.

Boiling Water Decoction (麻沸湯): This is used when food or drink causes deficiency-heat. Take its liquid — the steam is mild and detoxifying.

Green Silk Decoction (綠絲湯): It is also said to relieve toxicity and dry mouth. This substance belongs to the scallion family — boil it and take the juice. Its qi is mild and detoxifying.

Vapor Water (觀氣水): Produced from condensation inside a vessel or from ice-cold water collecting in a container. Take the drip from such vessels for use.

Sweat from Copper Vessels (銅器上汗): The moisture condensing on the surface of copper vessels, collected in the morning.

Cooking Water (炊湯): Do not use this to wash the face early in the morning, as it can cause skin blemishes. Water that has sat overnight in a copper vessel, collected in the morning from inside the pot — it nourishes the hair and promotes hair growth.

translation:
Six Celestial Qi

Taking it causes one to feel no hunger, to live long years, and to have a beautiful complexion and body. From the Classic of the Lingyang Master of Brightness.

[On the proper times:] In spring face south; in winter eat in stillness; the Mysterious Earth's Yellow-direction night qi is abundant; in summer eat the Six Qi of the Flying Spring.

[Those who practice:] The body gradually perceives change; the qi circulates; day by day one sheds [the old body]; those who take this qi will shed [the mortal form].

Earth Section

Earth governs all things; its ten-thousand uses; nine categories; ten mothers; eight mu; its nature is slightly warm, flavor is acrid and sour; it is said to be non-toxic; it can stop bleeding and disperse swellings.

Fulong Gan (Hearth Earth / Earth from beneath the kitchen stove)

[Its color is] slightly reddish-yellow. It promotes labor and delivery, brings down blood, stops bleeding from the channels, arrests uterine flooding. At night [applied] below; this is the earth taken from inside the stove, one chi below [the floor of the firebox].

[The stove earth:] The earth from within the furnace and stove, used as the principal earth; it can be used through the years for channel [disorders]; with children [it can be used for] night crying and convulsions. This is taken from one chi below inside the stove.

[True spirit earth:] The true spirit earth acts as the Fulong earth; it may be used year after year for channel disorders; with children for night crying.

East Wall Earth

[Take earth from the] east wall; [it is associated with] the Great Void and the true washing; and with the stove; [its] special quality is that the east wall is enduring and does not acquire toxicity; it governs and treats [disease].

[The east wall earth:] It is warm and harmonizing, benefits the liver and gallbladder; it acts as the Fulong [earth]; it may be used through the years.

[East wall earth:] It is the earth that first receives the morning light of the sun at the tiger hour [3–5 a.m.]; take it at that moment; it is used in the world for many southern [disorders].

West Wall Earth:
For those afflicted by smoke and fumes over years, it causes qi to descend. Take it from the western-facing wall where the sun shines at western-hour (late afternoon), from the damp reddish-white [soil], and use it to treat various ailments.

Good Yellow Earth:
[Combined with] pepper, it counters the toxins of wild mushrooms, relieves twisting abdominal pain. Its nature is balanced, taste sweet, non-toxic. It governs and is indicated for red and white dysentery.

For poisons from various substances, take soil from three chi (feet) depth or more downward. It also resolves toxins from food and various poisons. It governs red and white dysentery conditions.

Red Earth:
Apply it to cattle and horses; it disperses and eliminates epidemic diseases and stops all manner of bleeding. It is urgently used to kill pathogenic agents.

Its nature is warm, taste bitter, may be taken long-term, non-toxic. It can moisten the intestines and abdomen and stop dysentery.

White Chalk:
Its nature is warm; [use it] ground fine. Calcine it by burning with fire; it is non-toxic. It can moisten the intestines, stop dysentery.

Sea Gold Sand:
In the seventh month it promotes urination and treats sudden intestinal disorders. Gathered from a grass-like plant; collect the small pearl-like granules from plants about two chi tall.

translation:
Hundred Grasses Frost (Baekchoasang)
[A medicinal ash collected from the bottoms of pots used to burn plant matter.] It treats bleeding, promotes healing of flesh, and detoxifies. Used for postpartum hemorrhage, chronic bleeding disorders, and difficult deliveries. Also known as "furnace ink" (Nomo) or "village deep black." It resolves toxins, stops bleeding, and generates new flesh. It is non-toxic.

Furnace Ink (Nomo / Lú mò)
Stops bleeding from metal wounds [cuts]. Applied topically to wounds to generate flesh. Nature: slightly cold, non-toxic. Treats loss of consciousness from malignant influences, nosebleeds. Also known by the name "black fish tail" (Oryeo).

Beam Dust (Yangsangchin / Liáng shàng chén)
[Dust collected from the beams above a cooking fire.] It is gathered by scraping the beams where smoke has accumulated. Its nature is derived from the harmony between heaven and earth. It has long been used to supplement virtue and has the quality of being nourishing. It is mild in nature.

Grain Section (Gokbu)
Foods that can be eaten regularly, harmonizing the middle [digestive system]. Their nature is sweet and balanced, providing the highest nourishing virtues.

Sesame (Homa / Húmá)
Strengthens sinews and bones, moistens the five viscera, supplements deficiency, boosts essence (jing), extends lifespan, preserves youthful complexion, and fills the marrow. Nature: balanced. Flavor: sweet. Non-toxic. It boosts qi and strength, builds muscle and flesh, and nourishes the marrow.

The name Qingnang comes from ancient texts. According to various scholars' accounts, there are differing opinions. The black sesame (black芝麻) should be washed, the fat removed, and used to relieve itching.

Qingnang [Black Sesame]:
According to the Hujing (胡籍), sesame (Huma) is used daily in cooking. In spring it strengthens sinews and bones. It can be used to wash the hair. It is effective against cold disorders of the intestines. Sesame oil has a mild laxative effect.

Sesame Oil (胡麻油):
When roasted it can be mixed with other ingredients for internal use. It softens and lubricates the intestines, has a slightly cold nature. It is effective for intestinal conditions, against seasonal cold diseases, and soothes itching and promotes sleep.

White Sesame Oil (白油麻):
When roasted and processed, it can be used as food. There are two varieties; it lubricates the intestines and promotes blood circulation. The black variety dispels wind-cold-dampness.

Oil Sesame (油麻):
Today people use sesame oil, which is the same as huma. The white variety, when roasted, turns black.

Leaves:
The white leaves remove head-wind, moisten and harmonize, and promote hair growth. When roasted from the raw state, they turn black.

According to [the classical authority]: extremely difficult. Jingren (kernel): soak in hot water three times, [in] yin water until [husks loosen]. Difficult to use — remove the shell; water-soak successively, day by day, sun [dry], float two days, sun, break apart, let separate.

Violent drying — once fresh, intestinal dryness results. The intestine freshly cooked above — above hemp: take the kernel, soak in water, next day soak, complete [the process], break open.

Flower, upper [part], disperses [the three]. Membrane, leaf — use a knife to remove. Years — do not chain/restrain. Take the kernel, grain by grain, all intact. Take [the Korean prepared form], refined.

Seventh month, seventh day — harvest the finest. Seven people seeing [it go] mad in nature, running. [Korean name.] Acrid. One name: Ma-po-ji. Stops [this condition]. Refined.

Bean Yellow (Douhuan)
Soybean Yellow Sprouts (Dadou Huangjuan)
Adzuki Bean (Chi Xiaodou)

Bean Yellow: Used for sores and kidney conditions, it is a stimulating food. It benefits the pulse, supports kidney function, is sweet in flavor, governs the stomach, treats stomach heat and swelling. It stops [disease].

Soybean Yellow Sprouts:
The sprouts are grown from soybeans. The leaves are divided and one waits for the sprouts to emerge. It breaks open and the shoots come out. It is neutral in nature, sweet in flavor, and non-toxic. It governs wind-impediment and sinew cramping. Used in medicine, it is stir-fried lightly. [Korean source] ○ The sprouts are called Huangjuan.

Adzuki Bean:
The bean is long. The leaves are divided, waiting for the sprouts. It breaks open and the shoots emerge. Neutral in nature, sweet in flavor, non-toxic. It governs water swelling, lower body fullness, and promotes urination.

Flower and Leaf:

Flower: Also [used to make] wine. The soybean leaf is also called Huo (藿). It can be used to make soup and eaten. Neutral in nature, eliminates toxins, non-toxic, treats chronic illness, and is excellent. [Korean source] ○ One name is Qimei. It stops thirst and treats disease.

Leaf: The nature is neutral, eliminates toxins, non-toxic, treats chronic conditions, and is excellent. Stops thirst and treats disease.

[On adzuki bean properties:] When desiccated and parched, the qi acts to promote circulation. Adzuki beans, using early-ripening small varieties with bright reddish color, taken over time, detoxify. For those with toxic conditions, it governs water swelling, lower body fullness, and expels pus.

Harvest the adzuki bean in the seventh month, dry in shade.

translation:
Millet (粟米)

Millet: Its flavor is slightly salty with a mild taste; it is non-toxic. It nourishes kidney qi and removes heat from the spleen and stomach, benefiting qi. The smaller variety is called "liang millet" (梁粟); it resembles flesh in form, with small grains. The larger variety is called "rice millet" (稻), now called "liang." In the Poetry Classic's commentary, it is listed among the eight grains collectively. Among the eight grains, there is millet — as Zhu Xi states, this refers to the grain. The small variety is beneficial; all the larger ones are among the five grains. The word "millet" encompasses the grain within the husk. All are said to treat stomach heat, relieve thirst over three years, resolve toxins, and may be taken accordingly.

Aged Millet (陳粟米):
Its flavor is bitter. It mainly treats stomach heat, disperses irritability, stops diarrhea. Aged millet has a bitter flavor, hence it is called "aged millet." It clears stomach heat, relieves irritability, and promotes urination.

Millet Flour (粟米粉):
Its nature is cold, flavor sweet, non-toxic. It resolves irritability and heat, stops illness, and is good for treating skin inflammations (丹). It is regarded as an excellent medicine.

Parched Grain (糗):
Its nature is cold, flavor sweet, non-toxic. It resolves irritability and heat, stops thirst, and stops illness. It is one of the substantial major grains.

Millet Washing Water (粟米泔汁):
It is sour and sweet. It mainly treats cholera with irritability and thirst, and kills parasites. It is considered a good remedy.

translation:
[This page discusses the properties of several types of grain in traditional medicine:]

Glutinous Rice (糯稻秸/糯米):
Should not be consumed in excess. Eating it for a long time weakens the sinews and bones, makes people susceptible to illness, and prevents movement. It can aggravate old diseases. When used to brew wine, the wine becomes unsuitable for consumption. Wine brewed from glutinous rice is hot in nature and stirs the qi. Glutinous rice is cooling in nature. It is used by many people today; however, when brewed into wine it ferments differently. The glutinous variety is called "nuo" while the non-glutinous rice is coarser. Glutinous rice is cold in nature. It is used to regulate and treat the body, including illnesses such as wasting-thirst (diabetes), and its decoction is drunk to treat various conditions. When boiled, the liquid is consumed for therapeutic purposes.

Green Millet (青粱米):
Green millet is somewhat similar in appearance. It can be steamed and dried repeatedly. Its nature is slightly cold, with a very sweet flavor, and is non-toxic. It is mainly used to benefit the stomach, clear accumulated heat, and promote digestion. Green millet is superior to other grains in quality, being the cleanest and finest.

Yellow Millet (黄粱米):
White millet has a balanced nature, a sweet flavor, and is non-toxic. It benefits qi and harmonizes the middle burner. Its nature is slightly warming.

White Millet (白粱米)

Liang (粱) — Yellow millet (黃粱) is large with long hairs; is it not because it receives the balanced essence of the earth? It is the most fragrant and delicious among all grains. Its flavor is sweet and mild, it benefits the qi and nourishes the middle burner, but one should not eat it for too long or it will cause the person [harm].

Soft Rice (柔米)

When cooked, its nature is slightly cold, flavor is sweet, non-toxic; it benefits qi and nourishes the middle burner. One should not eat it for too long, as it may cause a person to sleep excessively.

Red Millet (丹黍米)

The black-stemmed variety: its nature is warm, flavor slightly bitter, non-toxic; the skin is reddish. It opens the passages, stops cough. The yellow-stalked variety also stops [cough].

Glutinous Millet (秫米)

The grain resembles millet but is smaller. Koreans call it "hwang" (yellow) and also refer to those stored [in jars]. It is good for making wine. The toxicity when cooked dissipates through the five grains' qi. This grain — people use it to make wine and also call the stored lees "yellow lees."
This is similar to millet in appearance but with smaller grains. Koreans call it "hwang" and also refer to those who store it. It is best used for wine-making.

translation:
Wheat (小麥)
Nature: slightly cold, balanced. Flavor: sweet. Non-toxic. Main uses: eliminates vexing heat, reduces thirst, stops dryness. All preparations use the whole grain.

It benefits urination; when the bran is removed, the flavor becomes warm. Wheat bran can dispel heat and is combined in decoctions to stop dryness and thirst.

Wheat is sown in autumn and ripens in summer, receiving the energy of all four seasons; thus small wheat naturally can eliminate heat, warm, and stop vexing heat.

It harmonizes the middle and regulates the qi. Wheat is sown in winter, grows through spring, blooms in summer, and ripens fully having received all four seasons' energies.

Fresh wheat, when the toxin has dissipated and the grain has been collected, harmonizes the nature of wheat, though it is not entirely sufficient for supplementing. Hence, among the five grains, wheat is considered precious; lingering varieties may also be spring-sown.

The flavor is warm and sweet, so it rarely has the power to supplement the middle and strengthen qi and fortify the stomach and intestines, giving strength and assistance.

Therefore, women who eat a lot of aged wheat — its nature is cold, its color is like learning — warming it can produce some toxicity, stirring wind and qi in the stones.

Those who eat it hot find it only rarely good. Aged starter (陳麴) has a warm nature and sweet flavor, useful for regulating and harmonizing cold; eating it daily reduces wind.

Noodles (麵)
Cold-food noodles (寒食麵): [A product made from] wheat or barley flour, taken and processed; it can be steamed and dispersed, relieving dysentery; used as noodles in two ways.

Ferment/Starter (麴)
Made in the sixth month; aids digestion. Also called 麴. Flavor sweet and balanced. Relieves dysentery, disperses noodle-based foods.

Divine Starter (神麴)
Aids digestion of water and grain, relieves dysentery. Nature: eliminates fullness. Flavor: used for red and white dysentery, epilepsy, and abdominal masses, and strengthens the spleen. Made in this month; good for digestion. Aged Korean wheat, made into noodle-starter, stops [ailments]; fish in the belly, no toxicity, eliminates scabies and tinea.

translation:
Barley (Chu/楚)
Barley: Roasted in a pan until fragrant, or stir-fried; helps with fullness in the stomach and chest, assists digestion, relieves food stagnation, and aids the flow of qi downward through the Yangming channel.

Red medicinal barley: Stir-fried until fragrant; activates blood circulation, aids digestion; stops doubt-difficult [i.e., difficult-to-treat] conditions. Taste: sweet; non-toxic. Regulates the middle burner, removes yang heat. The boiled barley's nature is cooling.

Also: roasted or fried barley. The nature is cold; it reduces fracture injuries and disperses blood stasis. The formula says: taste sweet, non-toxic, regulates the middle, removes heat. Boiled barley is cooling in nature.

Barley: stir-fried.

Floating Wheat (Fufu Xiaomai)
Floating wheat: Treats the heart; its nature is hot. Decocted together with jujube, it stops excessive sweating in women. Stops excessive sweating. Stir-fry and use it to stop excessive sweating.

Wheat Sprouts (Xiaomai Miao)
Wheat sprouts: Nature is greatly cold. Benefits the small intestine and reduces diaphragm heat. Wheat, during epidemic febrile disease and seasonal toxins, the sweat [is taken]; taken with alcohol, it counteracts the toxin, even if severe, preventing it from becoming [full-blown] wheat [disease].

Wheat Smut (Xiaomai Nu)
Wheat smut: Its nature is [cooling]; it is black in color. It is mainly used to treat fever, relieve irritability, benefit the small intestine and reduce heat, promote sweating, and counteract severe toxins, preventing their full development.

Jujube (Dazao)
Jujube: Its nature is warm, taste sour, non-toxic. It tonifies qi, warms the middle burner, and supplements the five deficiencies.

[The sprouts] turn black.

Weak persons: it strengthens those who are feeble. Eating it cooked benefits people; eating it raw causes coldness and harm. Large jujube: long-term consumption can cause the legs to become heavy and inhibit movement; over time it makes the body plump. [Excessive intake] may cause chest fullness.
